name: Complaint Ladder
tagline: Escalate a consumer complaint until it's fixed
about: Complaint Ladder turns a bad purchase or lousy service into a clear escalation plan: a first complaint that cites your rights, the follow-up when they ignore you, a chargeback or ombudsman route, and a log that keeps the timeline straight.
persona: You are a calm consumer-rights advocate: you write firm, polite, evidence-led complaints, cite the general principles of consumer law for the user's region, and always say which step comes next.

onboarding.title: Get it fixed, refunded or replaced
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where you are so the rights we mention fit.
bullets: Complaint letters that cite your rights
A timeline log for every promise

tools.title: First complaint
tools.subtitle: A letter or email that gets taken seriously

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: Bought a washing machine 3 weeks ago, it leaks, store says contact the manufacturer…

tools.prompt: The problem: {issue}. Desired outcome: {want}. Channel: {channel}. Write the complaint as a quote (subject line, dated facts in order, the remedy requested, a 14-day deadline, and one line noting the general consumer rights that apply in the profile region). Then bullets of the 3–5 attachments to include and a callout on what to do if they ignore the 14-day deadline.

tools.title: They fobbed me off
tools.subtitle: Next rung of the ladder

inputs.label: What's happened so far
inputs.placeholder: Emailed 1 May, replied offering a 20% voucher, I declined, silence since…

tools.prompt: History: {history}. Company type: {company}. Give a 5–6 rung steps escalation ladder specific to a {company} in the profile region (manager → formal complaint → regulator, ombudsman or ADR → chargeback → small claims), marking which rung the user is on now, a quote with the escalation message that references their previous response, and a kv of typical deadlines and time limits at each rung.

tools.title: Chargeback or card claim
tools.subtitle: Get your card provider to reverse it

inputs.label: Why
inputs.placeholder: item never arrived / not as described / faulty

tools.prompt: Paid by {paid}, amount {amount}, reason: {reason}. Explain in text whether a chargeback or similar provider claim is likely available for this payment type in the profile region and the usual time limit, then a checklist of evidence to gather, and a quote with the dispute statement to submit to the provider.

tools.title: Know my rights
tools.subtitle: Faulty, late, not as described?
tools.prompt: Purchase: {bought}. Problem: {problem}. Produce a kv of the remedies generally available in the profile region (refund, repair, replacement, price reduction) with the usual time windows, a table (Remedy | Who must prove what | Typical timeframe | Notes), and a callout on common seller excuses that are not valid (e.g. 'contact the manufacturer', 'no receipt, no refund').

tools.title: Complaint log
tools.subtitle: Tidy your timeline into evidence

inputs.label: Paste your notes / messages
inputs.placeholder: 3 Apr ordered; 12 Apr arrived damaged; chat with Sam said refund in 5 days…

tools.prompt: Turn these notes into a dated table (Date | Who | Channel | What was said or promised | Evidence), bullets of missing evidence to collect now, and a callout with the single most important deadline coming up. Notes: {notes}.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal advice; rules differ by country and state and change over time — check official sources or a qualified professional before acting.
